To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel fixed target for serial crystallographic experiments has been designed and implemented, and that a novel method for crystal registration has been developed, allowing for the first time a hit rate of 100% to be achieved.

a fixed-target crystal delivery system can be designed to deliver up to 11 259 crystals with high precision and that the use of a spectral mapping system allows for a 100% raw hit rate and an effective indexing rate approaching 50%.
a new crystallography micro-chip with a fiducial marker system for rapid, accurate crystal alignment and registration has been developed.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the optimization of the sample-delivery system and the development of methods for the rapid and accurate registration and alignment of crystals on a fixed-target chip, which are essential for the success of serial femtoseond crystallography at free-electron laser facilities.
the development of new methods for the efficient delivery and characterization of microcrystals for serial femtoseond crystallography.

the development of new methods for the delivery of crystals to X-ray beams, with the aim of improving the efficiency of data collection and the quality of data obtained from serial crystallograph­y experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fixed-target crystallographic chips developed here, combined with the spectral mapping approach, represent a highly efficient method for the delivery of crystals for serial femtoseond crystallography, and will enable the study of a broad range of proteins, including those that are not readily amenable to other sample-delivery methods.
the method presented here is a significant improvement over the previous generation of serial crystallographing devices.
the fixed-target crystallographic chip presented here has the capability to deliver a large number of protein crystals with a high hit rate and a high effective indexing rate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of a fixed-target sample-delivery system with spectral mapping of the crystals in the target is a highly efficient method for serial crystallographic experiments at X-ray free-electrons lasers.
we are approaching 100% raw hit rates with 50% effective indexing.
we have developed a new sample-delivery method for serial crystallographic experiments that allows the efficient use of the unique properties of X-ray free-electrons laser sources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of high spatial precision and a high hit rate can be achieved by a simple and robust method that does not require any complex hardware or software.
the use of fixed-target crystallographic chips in combination with spectral mapping allows for the rapid and efficient collection of data from a large number of crystals.
a fixed-target approach can be combined with spectral mapping to achieve high hit rates for serial femtoseond crystallography.
